entities.label: Place
entities.summary: The Jushi, or Gushi, were a people probably associated with the Subeshi culture, who established a kingdom during the 1st millennium BC in the Turpan basin. The kingdom included the area of Ayding Lake, in the eastern Tian Shan range. During the late 2nd and early 1st century BC, the area was increasingly dominated by the Han dynasty and the northern neighbours of the Jushi, the Xiongnu, and became one of the many minor states of the Western Regions of Han dynasty China. In 450 AD the Northern Liang destroyed the state of Jushi (車師) and occupied its capital city of Jiaohe (Yarkhoto). Jushi Kingdom is a historical country, established around 107 BCE.
